name: XPRS 1.5.0
body:
## XPRS 1.5.0 — one core for the phone and the station

The XPRS core now lives in its own repository ([xprs-dev/core](https://github.com/xprs-dev/core)) and runs unchanged in the app and in the [server edition](https://github.com/xprs-dev/server). 1.4.0's battery work came along: a phone on battery is still a messenger with a radio, and a full station only when plugged in.

### Web chat on the phone's hotspot
- **A blog post shows the moment it is published** (sending, published, or refused with Retry) instead of waiting for the archive's next write.
- **Formatted text** (XPRS.md 4.11): headings, bold, italic, lists, quotes and links, written beside a live preview with a packet counter. A line break travels as U+2028, a paragraph as U+2029.
- **Images by reference.** The browser shrinks a picture, hashes it and stores it on the phone (`/api/xprs/file/<ref>`); the post carries only the hash, so a radio link carries the words and whoever can fetches the picture.
- Stations host **rooms, a forum, alerts and moderation**, and share rooms across a **mesh of trusted stations**; the administrator sets the banner, logo, stylesheet and theme.

### The core
- Identity, transports, delivery, the archive, groups and the receive door are one plain-Dart package shared with the server. The screens forward intent and the core decides lanes and reach.
- The USB flasher, the transport core, preferences and i18n moved with it; `tool/arch_guard.dart` keeps UI out of it.
- When a transfer or a directed wire needs the shared transport, the core asks for a hub (`CoreHost.requestHub`, answered by `RnsSession`). A phone on battery still holds none otherwise.

### Battery (from 1.4.0, now in the core)
- Station when plugged in, normal on battery; the line lane to the archiver; a hub on request; the empty room's cheaper scan and beacon. See docs/performance.md 8.19–8.23.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/xprs-dev/app/compare/v1.4.0...v1.5.0
